name: Djupvik
description: A private housing project completed in 2023, designed by Arrhov Frick Arkitektkontor AB.

name: Väddö Veda
description: A private house project with a built area between 40-120 m2, currently under construction.

name: AF. 180 / GRISSLEHAMN / 1809
description: A private house proposal with a flexible area range of 40-120 m2.

name: Villa Toivonen
description: A 140 m² private house completed in Norrtälje, Sweden.

name: Atelier Lapidus
description: A 150 m² private house completed in 2016-2017, though specific materials and architectural features are not detailed in the available text.

name: Viggsö
description: A private house with a total area of 80 square meters, composed of three distinct sections of 40, 20, and 20 square meters.

name: Bredören
description: A private house of 80 m² designed by Arrhov Frick Arkitektkontor AB and documented through sketches and photographs by Mikael Olsson.

name: Lilla Rågholmen
description: A 100 square meter private house completed in the Stockholm Archipelago.

name: AF. 52 / NYKVARN / 1209
description: A private house with a total area of 145 square meters (100 + 30 + 15 m²) completed in 2014.

name: Townhouse
description: A narrow townhouse on a constrained site between old neighboring buildings, featuring three thin interior slabs that divide the open volume while maintaining continuous space that opens to the street, an intimate garden, and the sky.

name: Århus
description: A winning competition proposal for a townhouse on Jaegergårdsgade in Aarhus, Denmark.

name: House with a hidden atrium
description: A detached extension to a 1950s cabin featuring four volumes of varying heights arranged around a hidden central atrium, with blackened pine exterior cladding and plywood interior walls with strategically placed windows framing tree tops.

name: House in a horse field
description: A single-family house informed by rural farm buildings, positioned on a sloping site to offer panoramic views of Lake Vättern, with rooms arranged on stepped levels following the terrain and organized around a central vertical core containing the stairwell and wet rooms.

name: House with rope and ladder
description: A house in two parts consisting of a traditional brick volume with a gable roof and an enclosed circular garden, designed to create a calm private space while overlooking the sea on Sweden's southeast coast.

name: House for two artists
description: An extension to an older villa with a square footprint and cinderblock walls, featuring free-spanning glulam beams and sixteen skylights to create a flexible open atelier space, with pitch black tar felt cladding on the exterior contrasting the bright interior.

name: House for mother
description: A single-family dwelling and studio featuring a corrugated aluminum facade with wooden beams, plywood-lined walls, and concrete flooring, organized as two parallel gabled volumes that shift to emphasize the narrow plot.

name: House on Two Stairs
description: A narrow single-family house elevated on steel legs and balanced on two cast-in-place concrete stairs, featuring seven equally sized rooms separated by cross-laminated timber walls, with untreated wood panel and sheet metal roofing.

name: Surbrunnsgatan
description: A transformed 50 m² brick workshop converted into a small home featuring a partial second floor with exposed wood beams, Douglas veneer shelving, concrete flooring, and a deep green kitchen with whitewashed wood elements.

name: X
description: A competition entry for a modular house with a square footprint divided by a central X into four equal rooms, constructed from cross-laminated timber delivered as self-supported elements for on-site assembly.

name: Fritidshus i Tänndalen
description: A 130 sqm vacation house in the mountains with three bedrooms, a large living room with fireplace and valley views, plus a snowmobile garage and ski storage, featuring traditional Härjedalen-inspired interiors with green ceiling details and red woodwork combined with modern design.

name: Fritidshus i Bruksvallarna
description: A small vacation house with a timber upper volume in the X House system, iron vitriol-treated wooden facade, and a separate building for snowmobile storage, featuring sleeping loft, sauna, kitchen, and gathering spaces.

name: Bostadshus i Jämtlandsfjällen
description: A new red residential house in a mountain landscape that references the proportions and character of a previous dwelling on the site, with modern window placements and spatial arrangements designed for a family living close to nature.

name: Undrom
description: A modern vacation house with wood architecture, sedum roof, and extensive glazing toward the landscape, featuring 2.8-meter ceiling heights, concrete floors, and an iron vitriol-treated limber-clad facade.

name: The Dune Cabin
description: A low-lying summer house with a post-and-beam structure featuring corten steel infill panels, sawn pine walls, polished concrete floors, and discrete glass elements that blur the boundary between interior and exterior.

name: Villa Butter
description: A heavy, modern villa situated on a cliff overlooking the ocean and within a grove, designed with oak, concrete, glass, and copper materials, featuring a blurred boundary between interior and exterior spaces with deep blue accents.

name: STENEN&ENEN
description: A raw experimental house featuring stones and junipers in a foggy setting, for which the firm prepared building permits, construction drawings, and executed the project.

name: Ö17
description: A house for an art collector designed as a formalized vision integrating architecture and art, situated within an old stone quarry on Gotland with spaces that function as a gallery, featuring a material palette balanced between perfection and imperfection that frames views and creates tectonic phenomena.

name: Djupvike
description: An artist's combined home and studio compound of five single-story structures featuring concrete, treated pine wood, and plaster, with playful interior details including pink apricot marble terrazzo and blue painted ceilings, positioned on a rocky cove overlooking the Baltic Sea.

name: Savannen 8
description: A rectangular house built from prefabricated concrete walls with raw concrete and plywood interiors, featuring a facade created through a custom method developed with a local concrete factory and incorporating industrial-inspired details like a kitchen fan made from a galvanized steel foot grate.

name: Villa Fjällsvik
description: A private villa on a rocky archipelago island featuring a modest sea-facing façade that replaces a former cottage, with a larger northwestern wing tucked into the landscape, designed with materials and craftsmanship inspired by the seaside context.

name: Sahara
description: A summer cottage built from local materials by local artisans, elevated on light stilts over the forest floor with a pine facade, designed as a simple yet sophisticated structure in the threshold between forest and sea.

name: Villa BM
description: A summer house designed as an enclosed courtyard villa that creates a sense of seclusion and intimacy, with tall pine trees from the surrounding forest visible above the property walls, making the residence feel isolated within the forest.

name: Pine House
description: A summer house completed in 2024 featuring a visible timber construction with handcrafted detailing, sited on a north-facing slope in sparse forest and designed to honor authentic, tactile experiences through natural materials and legible structural expression.

name: Sommarhus S
description: A summer house completed in 2025, designed by Johan Sundberg Arkitektur with carpentry by Kasper Thulin.

name: Villa HDV
description: A family home featuring contrasting materials that express varying degrees of intimacy, surrounded by carefully planned garden rooms and landscape on all sides.

name: Sommarhus E
description: A single-family vacation house on Gotland built with local wood, glass, limestone, and concrete in a Nordic mid-century bungalow style that sits low to the ground and uses narrow ribbons of slow-growth pine to integrate with its natural surroundings.

name: BV50
description: A modern family home in a coastal pine forest designed with a unified material palette of brick, glass, wood, and Baltic limestone, featuring flexible spaces that adapt as the family grows and carefully balanced transitions between shared and private areas.

name: Yngsjö
description: A family summer house for four people featuring a north-south oriented volume with a sheltered western terrace, with the southern section grounded and the northern section elevated on slender pillars, clad in larch panel with oak interior finishes and larch ceiling.

name: Villa MSV
description: A residence designed for a couple with accommodations for guests and family, positioned among tall pine forest with two distinct garden spaces oriented to morning sun and west-facing areas for sitting and dining.

name: Sommarhus Solviken
description: A three-bedroom summer house elevated on twelve steel columns on a steep slope with sea views, featuring wood facade panels, muted green tones, black-lacquered aluminum windows and doors, and large sliding glass doors opening to a wraparound balcony.

name: Sommarhus T
description: A summer house for a family with two children composed of three interconnected volumes with a large shared shallow hipped roof, featuring a timber frame with steel elements and natural larch and stained spruce, designed to appear modest from outside while providing generous interior spaces and nature contact in all directions.

name: Villa Tennisvägen
description: A family residence designed as two brick volumes and one aluminum-clad volume arranged in a U-shape around an inner courtyard, featuring black brick, dark gray aluminum, oak and cedar wood interiors, and natural stone accents.

name: Sommarhus H
description: A vacation house on the south coast of Skåne, clad in specially designed larch wood panel treated with silicate-based wood protection, featuring shadow play from battens on the facades and opening toward water views with separate compartments of varying depth and window placement.

name: Villa J
description: A generous family villa with three children's bedrooms featuring a central atrium courtyard, with a timber and steel frame structure and facades clad in Danish brick, light gray plaster, dark-stained pine, and black-painted aluminum.

name: Bergman-Werntoft
description: A private residence inspired by traditional Scanian-Danish atrium houses, featuring a masonry exterior wall and largely glazed interior façade, with steel-reinforced timber construction on a concrete slab, black-painted light concrete walls, and Siberian larch cladding, designed to blur the boundary between interior and nature through a year-round winter garden and flush floor transitions.

name: Villa Syrstad
description: A family residence designed in harmony with its coastal landscape, featuring generous glazing on the west and south facades, covered terraces, and a brick fireplace dividing the living spaces, with private bedroom areas at each end.

name: Sommarhus Akenine
description: A summer house nestled in the forest on the south coast of Skåne, Sweden, featuring a distinctive timber deck structure resting on three concrete beams, with light timber and glass walls clad in Siberian larch panels and three-layer lamellar boards, designed to open toward the sea while providing shelter from the forest side.

name: Sommarhus Sandby
description: A 167 m² summer house for a family of five with wood-clad façades and roof in treated Siberian larch, featuring open-plan living spaces with sliding glass walls that connect to the surrounding forest and garden.

name: Villa Ljung
description: A residential villa on a double plot near the sea, consisting of three timber-clad buildings with facades of Siberian larch in varying qualities, Danish hard-fired tile floors, and rooms organized around a large central living space with a fireplace and adjoining winter garden.

name: Villa Lima
description: A 1.5-story modern villa with a traditional pitched roof, featuring large glass sections, dark gray matte facade with mixed-width smooth-planed wood, steel-reinforced timber construction, and an open floor plan that preserves existing trees on the property.

name: Villa Håkansson-Tegman
description: A single-story modern house designed around an inner courtyard with Danish atrium house origins, clad in light Danish brick with a steel-reinforced timber frame, featuring extensive window placements and aluminum profiles to maximize connection with nature and light.

name: House V
description: A three-level private home on a cliff overlooking Djurgården featuring exposed cast-in-place concrete and dark brick exterior, with oak floors and limestone interiors, organized with open living spaces on the top level and more intimate rooms below.

name: House on a Hill
description: A three-level private residence entirely cast in concrete and anchored to exposed bedrock, featuring a distinctive rotated floor plan with folded facades that create wind-shielded terraces and origami-like visual effects while merging indoor and outdoor spaces to emphasize views over the Stockholm archipelago.

name: House on a Hillside
description: A private home laid out as six stepped and staggered blocks that follow the natural topography, featuring exposed concrete blocks (referencing local barn construction) with large infrequent window openings and a linear interior passage connecting varied spatial sequences.

name: Garden House
description: A 180 m² wooden private home on a Mälaren lakefront site with a triangular footprint driven by topography, wrapped in a trellis supporting vines and seven plant species to create vertical gardens, featuring a two-storey winter garden and open-plan ground floor with a roof terrace.

name: Archipelago House
description: A lightweight 130 m² summer vacation house in wood and glass with a black-stained exterior, white-painted interior, and extensive glazing that creates reflective interactions between interior space and the surrounding archipelago landscape.

name: Red House
description: A private residence with a symmetrical pitched roof and Falu red-stained wooden façade, featuring a solid Swedish timber load-bearing structure and layered plywood panels that create a three-dimensional shingle-like effect, designed to complement the early 18th-century cultural heritage buildings on the site while offering contemporary living spaces inside.

name: Atrium House
description: A vacation home built as a low wall around an enclosed atrium courtyard, featuring masonry with natural plaster tinted with carbon black, oxidised zinc metal components, and tar oil-treated oak doors and windows that grey naturally over time.

name: Husarö
description: A vacation home with a pitched roof and open spatial plan, clad entirely in folded black sheet metal, with wood construction including glulam beams and plywood vaults, positioned on a clearing overlooking the sea in the Stockholm archipelago.

name: Engberga - ThamVidegård
description: A three-level private home on a Stockholm archipelago peninsula featuring a solid concrete base, a glazed middle floor with open pillars, and a top floor clad in burnt wood (Shou sugi ban), organized around curved concrete walls and a central wooden box containing stairs, fireplace, and storage.

name: House K
description: A thin residential block in Stocksund featuring cut-outs for light, double-height voids, and a roof terrace, with façades of stained black plywood panels mounted on a slow-grown pine framework and an exposed concrete entrance canopy.

name: Söderöra
description: A lightweight summer house on a remote Stockholm archipelago island built from wood and glass materials transported by boat, organized around a top-lit central room with four corner rooms and finished with black bitumen slate roof and natural wooden panels.

name: Villa Gislöv
description: A single-floor seaside villa with brick walls providing rhythm and stability, a flat lightweight roof with overhangs for sun protection, and strategically placed glass and wood sections that maximize southern views while providing privacy toward the north and courtyard.

name: Villa Siblings
description: Two sister houses with a shared central concrete wall and solid timber frame, featuring free-form geometry, open family rooms with varying ceiling heights, and minimalist interiors with unfinished wood and exterior larch cladding.

name: House Djurö
description: A cast in situ concrete house perched on a cliff overlooking the Stockholm Archipelago, featuring flanking walls that frame views toward the sea, stained spruce timber windows and doors, a large concrete terrace with frameless glass balustrade, a custom pool, and interiors with concrete walls and floors complemented by stained oak paneling and stainless steel kitchen elements.

name: Björhövda House
description: A private house in a forest clearing with a wooden facade clad in Organowood that grays over time, featuring a diagonal floor plan that creates unexpected spatial qualities and views toward a nearby lake and surrounding forest.

name: Smallholding at Nesjestranda
description: An extension and remodeling of a smallholding on Norway's northwest coast, featuring oiled dense pine cladding with tapered boards for filtered light, a stepped roofline clad in aluzinc that follows the terrain, and a new entrance with cast concrete flooring and wood stove heating.

name: Chr Tomters veg
description: An expansion of a traditional red-painted wooden house into a spatially complex residence for a large family, with two new volumes linked by transitional spaces and featuring a material palette of reds in timber cladding, brick, and tiles alongside interior finishes of ash wood, painted surfaces, brick, and concrete.

name: Cabin Nordmarka
description: A small retreat cabin with an open, light interior featuring a multi-level layout that ascends from entrance to living, recreational, sleeping, and children's areas, designed to minimize environmental impact through a steel bolt foundation system and positioned to maximize views of sunset, woods, and lakes while respecting an adjacent 1930s cabin.

name: Cabin Ulvik
description: A cabin designed as homage to country-road architecture, featuring ochre-yellow walls that camouflage into the aspen forest, a thick protective southern wall facing prevailing winds and rain, and a facade composition that blends vernacular farmhouse and barn design traditions.

name: Kvinaosen
description: A single family house designed by Rever & Drage AS in 2021.

name: Zieglers Nest
description: A tall, slender single-family house built on a steep site with a framework ground floor and log construction upper floors, featuring oak and pine staircases, south-facing views of the Molde fjord panorama, and a five-meter high utility room with flood lighting on the ground level.

name: 1/3 Hus
description: A detached single-family house with two insulated floors of 50 square meters each, featuring a large uninsulated utility space under an extended roof supported by tilted glulam columns, designed for affordability and future expandability as the owners' family grows.

name: Trolltind
description: A robust mountain cabin built with high-quality traditional craftmanship and local timber, arranged as a connected row of differently-constructed buildings featuring a glassed-in garage, laundry area, kitchen, living room with barrel vault ceiling and panorama window, bedrooms, and workspace, designed for active outdoor families with drying facilities and panoramic mountain views.

name: House Øksendal
description: A detached single-family house with a simple exterior and complex interior featuring a tractor and ATV garage, gym, cheese and wine cellar in the bedrock, wood-fired water heating system, and a kitchen with a five-meter-high ceiling and large south-facing windows, organized around a central staircase.

name: Cabin Årsund
description: A residential cabin combining a traditional gabled roof structure with modernist flat-roofed modules, featuring a sheltered main volume with bedrooms and a west-facing study module with ocean views, connected to a pre-existing annex.

name: Feisteinveien
description: An addition to a single-family house featuring a large northern extension with two small bedrooms, living room, and combined home-cinema-and-exercise room with classical skylight, along with a smaller southern extension for bathroom and entrance, designed to preserve the original building as the central element with contrasting color.

name: Pedervegen
description: An addition to a 1962 Scandinavian functionalist detached house featuring wood cladding in colors derived from the original brick walls, with quarter-circle forms and distinctly zoned bathroom and bedroom spaces designed to capture specific light and views of the surrounding mountains.

name: Furukollen
description: A single-family house for four people integrated between granite outcrops, featuring a coal-burned brick ground floor anchored to bedrock, a lightweight timber upper floor, a long ridge beam with clerestory window, and interior surfaces clad in knot-free pine panelling with custom Norwegian pine joinery.

name: Sykkylven
description: A single-storey building that meanders between trees, responding to the landscape, vegetation, and surrounding views.

name: Long House on Pillars
description: A 115 sqm residential house for a ceramicist and scientist, raised on wooden pillars to preserve the existing landscape, featuring exposed wooden beams and pine walls with recycled brick floors, set between rocks and trees with a simple open floor plan separated by sliding doors.

name: Brick house with tower
description: A 220 sqm single-family house with a tower featuring loadbearing wooden construction clad in coal-fired red, brown and ochre Danish brick, with copper fittings and ash windows, organized across three stories with long views through the interior and overlooking Lake Mjøsa.

name: House in Red Concrete
description: An intergenerational three-generation family home built with prefabricated red iron oxide-pigmented concrete elements designed for partial owner self-construction, featuring exposed concrete ceilings, pine paneling in the kitchen and living areas, and a flexible interior layout adapted to a steep hillside site.

name: Cabin Rones
description: A small residential cabin with a compact concrete base and triangular cross-laminated timber upper floor wrapped in black roofing felt, featuring raw concrete walls, polished concrete floors, Norwegian pine interiors, and an open glass facade facing the fjord.

name: Lofoten house
description: A single-family house with wood construction on a concrete base and steel cladding.

name: Corbus Nephew
description: Renovation and extension of a single-family house from 1940, allegedly built by Le Corbusier's nephew, Mr. Eduard Jaquet.

name: Atelier Aksnes
description: A self-built 20 sqm atelier designed for a ceramicist.

name: T House
description: A villa reinterpreting the traditional Trønderlåna with three wings creating two outdoor spaces, featuring a wooden frame construction in birch plywood and charred pine boards under an aluminium roof.

name: House14a
description: A 1951 post-war single-family house with red brick façade and gable roof, transformed through traditional architectural techniques like exposing, covering, cutting, and joining to create a non-hierarchical collage of old and new elements.

name: House on Fanø
description: A contemporary reinterpretation of the traditional Fanø longhouse that combines local building traditions with modern construction, featuring robust materials and sensory qualities while maintaining the east-west orientation and simple structure characteristic of the island's historic dwellings.

name: Sankt Knuds Vej
description: An extension on a private house in Frederiksberg designed in collaboration with office kim lenschow.

name: House in Mols Hills
description: A 175 sqm summer residence with four interconnected 'house-shaped' units around a central courtyard, featuring oiled cedar boards, sliding shutters, and floor-to-ceiling windows that blur interior-exterior boundaries.

name: Tagestorp
description: A private house in Gentofte designed by pihlmann in collaboration with office kim lenschow.

name: Villa Tambar
description: A 220 m² house featuring an inviting ground floor paired with a more secluded upper level to establish dedicated spaces for everyday life.

name: Garden House
description: A distinctive addition to a multi-generational home that encloses a shared courtyard anchored by a majestic oak tree, with a size of 160 m².

name: House at Nøtterøy
description: A new family house cut into the landscape that blends with its surroundings, with a size of 170 m².

name: A31-A
description: A compact family house of 123 m² where two spaces connected by a long wall make up the main living area.

name: Hus på Valderøya
description: A renovation and expansion of a 1973 villa featuring three cast concrete elements that shield from westerly winds, large glazed doors opening to views of Alnes lighthouse, and interior finishes in ash, solid oak, and pine combined with exposed laminated timber.

name: Hytte i Hol
description: A renovation and extension of a vacation house featuring a new addition with bedrooms and a separate living room, with matching wood panel and details that harmonize with the original structure and a sheltered outdoor area.

name: Green Villa Margo
description: A mass timber single-family house with CLT structures, dark-green-painted facades, zinc roof, natural ventilation, and interior finishes of light spruce and dark red terracotta tiles, designed to nestle around an existing knoll with preserved vegetation.

name: Palapa De Oro
description: Fourteen primitive yet luxurious holiday homes made in local clay and timber, offering space for silence, simplicity and relaxation.

name: Cubiculum
description: A timeless residential haven inspired by the Roman domus, featuring natural haptic materials of wood and clay in a technology-free environment designed for rest and peaceful living.

name: Villa in the archipelago
description: A holiday villa in the Finnish archipelago built with massive CLT wooden walls and slabs, featuring natural gravity ventilation, a detached foundation slab, visible bearing roof structure, and large windows creating a close relationship between interior and exterior spaces.

name: Villa Koppar
description: A fully ecological, geothermically heated passive house for a young family constructed with a prefabricated straw structure (Ecococon), featuring spruce board cladding, clay plaster interiors, rammed earth floors, and a roof with bio-based color-coated steel with rapeseed oil coating.

name: Villa Ris
description: A 320 square meter villa completed in 2025.

name: Villa Solveien
description: A 350 m² intimate family home designed for a steep hillside site, featuring a structural division of a heavy concrete base with light timber construction above, a central oak staircase, and materials chosen for durability and timeless quality.

name: Ullernkollen
description: A residential project of approximately 220 m² completed in 2024 in Oslo, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: Villa Berg
description: A 390 m² single-family house with a narrow facade to the street and elongated form following the terrain, featuring cast-in-place concrete with red pigment, red brick, copper, and oak materials, with an internal atrium bringing light through vertical connections.

name: Villa Nes Terrasse
description: A 350 m² single-family villa featuring a horizontal roof plane with integrated technical installations, closed wooden boxes defining interior spaces, and a gabion retaining wall that anchors the structure into the sloped terrain.

name: Villa Bruksveien
description: A 340 m² villa completed in 2024, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: Villa Bombakken
description: A 400 m² villa completed in 2022 in Lysaker, Bærum.

name: Villa Dagaliveien
description: A 550 m² villa completed in 2022, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS and built by Gunnar Johansson.

name: Villa Bjerkealleen
description: A compact rectangular house with a sloped roof, brick base and red-painted wood panel facade, featuring a central dining room, multiple living spaces, and outdoor terraces positioned on sloping terrain with two stories plus a basement level.

name: Villa Slemdalsvingen
description: A single-family house of 350 m² featuring brick façades with oak details and a volumetric form that responds to neighboring architecture while creating multi-level outdoor spaces oriented toward the south.

name: Villa Trosterudveien
description: A single-family home composed of four distinct volumes with pitched roofs, featuring concrete foundation, timber frame construction, standing wood cladding on façade and roof, with an attached garage and glass-clad greenhouse, designed to respect the scale of the surrounding residential area while adapting to the sloped terrain.

name: Villa Gyssestadkollen
description: A single-family house on a south-facing slope with two stories plus a basement level, featuring a triangular floor plan that optimizes views and noise protection, with concrete and white concrete construction in the atrium and dark copper cladding on the main floors.

name: Villa Snarøya
description: A approximately 350 m² villa with a pitched roof, positioned to maximize fjord views and southern light, featuring a façade that combines cedar wood, aluminum, and glass, with open-plan living spaces on the ground floor and bedroom areas on upper levels.

name: Hytte Budor
description: A 120 m² vacation house completed in 2025, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: 3PR Hytta
description: A compact 70 m² vacation cabin with loft space designed as a modular prototype that combines architectural quality, flexibility, and sustainability through a 3x3 unit planning system that can be mirrored and rotated to adapt to different sites and orientations.

name: Vinterro
description: A pair of cabins of 110 m² and 140 m² completed in 2024 at Kvitfjell.

name: Hytte Ostøya
description: A 110 m² vacation house completed in 2025, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: Hytte Nøtterøy
description: A 90 m² cabin completed in 2024, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: Hytte Kvitfjell
description: A 260 m² cabin completed in 2024, designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: Hytte Portør
description: A 75 m² completed vacation house designed by R21 Arkitekter AS.

name: Sand Paviljong
description: An 80 m² pavilion-like cottage with exposed oak columns outside the glass façade, concrete foundation, flexible wooden shutters, and an open-air kitchen concept that can be fully opened in summer.
